prompt: The α-hydrogen of a ketone has pKa ~20, dramatically more acidic than an ordinary sp³ C–H (pKa ~50). Why?

options.label: The enolate anion is resonance-stabilized with negative charge on the adjacent carbonyl oxygen.
The α-carbon is sp² hybridized and the extra s-character makes its H more acidic.
The α-position has reduced steric strain, releasing bond energy on deprotonation.
Hyperconjugation from the C=O donates into the C-H σ*, polarizing the bond.

explanation: Deprotonation gives an enolate: the negative charge delocalizes from the α-carbon onto the carbonyl oxygen via resonance. Oxygen is much happier holding the charge → huge stabilization → much weaker conjugate acid (lower pKa). The α-C is still sp³ in the ketone; sp² is only after deprotonation (in the enolate itself).
